waypoints.name: Rainy Pass PCT North Trailhead
waypoints.note: SR-20 milepost ~159, ~2 mi east of Rainy Pass; NPS backcountry permit required for overnight camping, $5/day USFS parking fee, no potable water on site.
waypoints.directions: Park at the Rainy Pass PCT North trailhead on SR-20 near milepost 159, about two miles east of Rainy Pass. A $5-per-day USFS parking fee applies here, and there's no potable water on site. An NPS backcountry permit is required for overnight camping in the Goode Glacier/moraine camp zone; reserve it in advance at the Wilderness Information Center in Marblemount.

waypoints.name: PCT / North Fork Bridge Creek Trail junction
waypoints.note: Leave the Pacific Crest Trail here and turn onto the North Fork Bridge Creek Trail toward Goode's north side.

waypoints.name: Grizzly Creek crossing
waypoints.note: Usually an easy log crossing but reported as a dangerously high, hard-to-find ford in early season; trail turns brushy/overgrown just beyond it.

waypoints.name: Lateral moraine camp above Goode Glacier
waypoints.note: Established bivy atop the lateral moraine overlooking the Goode Glacier's seracs; standard base camp for the Southwest Couloir attempt.

waypoints.name: Goode Glacier crossing
waypoints.note: Cross the glacier from the moraine camp to reach the couloir base; route-finding is tricky and late-season snow bridges can be deteriorated.

waypoints.name: Black Tooth Notch
waypoints.note: Foot-wide notch gained by an exposed class 4 traverse (fixed sling marks the crux step); rock here is loose/"garbage" — watch for rockfall onto climbers below.

waypoints.name: Goode Mountain summit
waypoints.note: Highest point in North Cascades National Park; summit block above the notch adds exposed class 4-5 moves before the true top.

wa_goode_mountain_southwest_couloir.approach: From the Bridge Creek/PCT trailhead on SR-20 near milepost 159 (Rainy Pass area, ~4,875 ft), follow the Pacific Crest Trail southbound along Bridge Creek. This stretch loses elevation steadily — roughly 2,000 ft over about 9.5-9.6 miles — down through forest to the North Fork Camp junction, where the PCT crosses Bridge Creek (a footbridge here has been washed out in past years; check current NPS conditions before counting on it). At the junction, turn onto the North Fork Bridge Creek Trail and head upstream (north); this climber's/stock trail is roughly 7 miles long and regains about 1,700 ft, but grows progressively brushier and less maintained the farther up-valley you go, with alder and overgrowth becoming a real time sink in late summer. The trail eventually peters out in the big cirque below Goode, Storm King, and Mount Logan — most parties leave the maintained tread around mile 13-14 of the approach to ford the North Fork (a cold, sometimes knee-deep crossing; easier a short way upstream near a cairn) and pick up an intermittent boot path/cairns through talus and alder ('tunnel' sections of brush) toward the toe of the Goode Glacier. From there it's off-trail travel over moraine and glacier remnants (light crampons/axe useful if there's residual snow or open crevasses) to a rotten, blocky ridge that accesses the base of the couloir proper — expect loose, moving rock underfoot on this last stretch. Reasonable bivy options exist near the glacier toe (~6,400-6,800 ft, limited flat tent sites) or higher on ledges closer to the couloir base. Total approach is commonly done as a long day-plus-camp, on the order of 15-16 miles and 4,000-4,800 ft of gain to high camp; water is generally available at regular intervals along Bridge Creek and its tributaries but can be scarce higher up near camp, so fill up at the last reliable stream.
